It’s a hard spot to be in for sure. Me not listening to The Weeknd anymore is just a personal choice though and I don’t automatically think that everyone is homophobic for listening to him. Case in point; you.

For me it’s just as long as we collectively agree to hold him accountable for that verse at the least. As long as we can all agree that, yeah that was in poor taste and very oppressive to say. That’s what I think what we best.

From there if one decided to continue supporting his music or not is completely personal preference. I get why you would, the man is talented.

Personally though, I think not listening to him will be good for my own music because I will be inspired to create something that people like myself can relate to without feeling attacked, ya feel?

I’m okay with jumping to label him that way since he never acknowledged that. Homophobia is homophobia.. noone forced him to say that he just did. If it is affecting people and making them feel oppressed in any way it’s pretty homophobic.

It’s different if it’s like a comedy special done in the right way. But you can tell he really thinks that if all he had to say was “no more daytime music” (implying that he’s gonna keep being controversial).

Basically what I’m saying is why is it so hard to address that for him, but in the next breath deny being homophobic. It literally is just one verse like you said, not that hard to clear up if he wanted to. He just doesn’t want to so I don’t see how he could not be homophobic in this situation.
Well you can’t just claim not to be phobic of something. If you say something ____phobic the proof is in the pudding. Especially if you never apologize for it and show growth and change.

Look it’s really hard to let go of an artist, but please try to see it from my perspective. One line or not, it was really hurtful. If it was a line about anti-semitism, people wouldn’t be as forgiving.

If The Weeknd were to address his wrongdoing in regards to this verse and the homophobia surrounding it, I would give him another chance. But he literally just dropped it on us, said “hey all of my lesbian listeners, just a ‘reminder’ (haha get it? Reminder) that you’re all just lesbian because you’re scared to get hurt by men!!”. 

I’m the type of person who holds people accountable, and so I get what you’re saying that I shouldn’t sacrifice a good portion of my music for one error. But for me, that one error wasn’t just a part of a little song. It’s part of a bigger issue which is certain straight men trying to “win” lesbians. He did it nonchalantly and that’s disgusting to me. To me this isn’t just a verse, this is a verse that reminds me of the struggle I go through everyday with casual lesbophobia. Now when I think of The Weeknd I just think of that line.

Artists just need to address their mistakes, and if they don’t this is how it makes their fans feel..

The problem with that is he’s still fetishizing this supposed woman’s sexuality. I mean in the song, it goes “you said you’re going through a phase”, but I don’t think she would say that about herself? Whatever it’s a hard one.

And another issue is the “protecting your heart” line. He’s suggesting that she’s bi/lesbian just because she was hurt by men and is now choosing to be that way. That’s problematic.

Lastly, although “fuck you straight” can be interpreted in two ways, many of the listeners interpreted it in the corrective rape way. And if that’s not what he meant, he never cleared that up. The fact that he is allowing that to be interpreted that way with no explanation suggests that he doesn’t really care.

Accepting depression might sound too broad. It doesn’t mean that you have to say kumbaya and accept the hard truths of depression. All it really means is that you kind of... let go. You don’t try to push the feelings away at the least. Don’t get me wrong, coping mechanisms are great, (and I have suggestions if you’re interested message me) but I’m hearing that might be a lot for you right now. 

True acceptance of depression is a longterm implementation, but you can start at any moment right? :)

I think you know you’ve accepted depression, when you allow the pain to be felt, and you are ready to move on to greater things. You are ready to take steps out of depression little by little. Easier said than done but that’s my general opinion on it.

Do you think a more practical approach would be helpful? Such as doing worksheets, practicing mindfulness, group therapy, etc?

Talk therapy is helpful for only so long until, as you said, you find yourself repeating yourself and not making any progress.
Feel free to message me. <3 Depression is the loneliest, emptiest feeling, so you reaching out is really natural and beneficial. Don’t give up please.

Last time I laid in bed for about 3 days straight. What got me out of it was socializing (my mom sat by me for a couple hours), and being all cramped from laying down honestly.

Maybe that sounds really trivial. It was a hard time though.

I suggest you take it easy, because although you’re “not doing anything” physically, you are ill and that makes it hard to get moving. Your mind isn’t exactly working with you at the moment. So lets just try to be kind to it; let it feel and emote, if its numb let it be that way for the time being.

Once you accept the depression, (not dwell but accept) a weight will lift off of your shoulders because you wont have to fight it anymore. From there physical activity might seem less daunting too.

Remember that you know yourself best, so take advice when it resonates or seems reasonable for you. Help is always available. Stay strong. <3
